body: The listing prints what is not in the jar: no fillers, no preservatives, and a vegan capsule rather than gelatin. It does not print the name of a single plant in the formula.
The serving is two capsules a day with meals. The capsule count and the milligrams in a capsule are not printed.
Two capsules a day, with a meal.
Two a day is the printed serving, and the small print says not to exceed the stated dose. If a day is missed, take two the next day rather than four.
Not printed on the listing. Dry, out of direct sun and lid on is what we would do with any capsule. No fridge.
Not for children. If you are pregnant or breastfeeding, or you take prescribed medication, ask your GP or pharmacist before you start.
No fillers is a useful sentence and it is not the list. Without the list, this jar cannot be checked against a prescription by anybody, including us.
Sent out from 599 Smithdown Road, Liverpool, Tuesday to Sunday. UK delivery is free over £50, or you can collect from the shop between 10 and 6, any day except Monday.

ingredients.intro: Three things, all of them about what the jar is not: not animal, not farmed, not padded out. The listing prints 100% vegan, wildcrafted botanicals, and no fillers or preservatives. It does not print the name of one plant in the formula, so the frames below are empty rather than filled with a species we have picked to suit the front of the jar.

cards.p: No plant is named on this listing, in Latin or in English, and no part of a plant is named either. We are not going to work backwards from the product name, and we are not going to copy a list from another shop selling something with a similar name.

cards.p: This one is worth reading carefully. A jar can tell you truthfully what is not inside it while telling you nothing about what is. Both sentences belong on a label, and only one of them is here.

doctrine.h3: We publish the specification. We do not publish claims about what it does.
doctrine.p: Everything printable about this jar is above, and most of it is a sentence about something we do not have. The page carries no line about what the formula is for and no expansion of the word on the front, because that word is a name we chose and not a description of anything.

spec.intro: What the listing states, including the two things it states are absent, and every row where it states nothing at all.

reiss.label: From Reiss
reiss.h2: What is not in it is the easy half
paras: No fillers, no preservatives. I stand behind that sentence, it is checkable, and any manufacturer can be held to it. It is also the easy half of a label. The hard half is the list of what is actually in the capsule, in Latin, with the part of the plant named, and that half is missing from this listing.

I have left the ingredient frames on this page empty for that reason. Filling them with a plausible plant would have made the page look finished, and it would have been an invention. The people who most need the list are the ones on a prescription, and they need the real one or nothing.

So the sheet prints the serving, the price, the capsule and the two absences, and stops. If you want to know what is in the jar before you buy it, ring the shop and somebody will go and read the sack to you. When the list is printed on the label it goes on this page in full.
reiss.pull: A jar can tell you truthfully what is not in it and still not tell you what is.
